newsitem.title: VIETNAM: Vietnam sees chance for talks on spat with China.
newsitem.headline: Vietnam sees chance for talks on spat with China.

text.p: Vietnam is hoping to hold talks with China this week on competing claims to an offshore area where a Chinese oil rig has been drilling, Foreign Minister Nguyen Manh Cam said on Monday.
"I hope this week. Perhaps in Hanoi," Cam told Reuters in response to a question on the timing and location for talks which Vietnam has requested as a solution to the dispute.

Cam was speaking after a meeting with visiting Thai Prime Minister Chavalit Yongchaiyudh, who told a news conference on Sunday that it was not Thailand's place to take a position on the bilateral dispute.
Thai diplomats said they believed that senior Vietnamese officials had not raised the issue during Chavalit's 24-hour visit because a Vietnam-China meeting on the dispute was imminent.
"We heard unofficially that China has agreed to send an expert team to Vietnam to discuss the issue this week," one said.
Last week, Vietnam restated its claim to the area of the South China Sea, which is some 64.5 nautical miles off its central coast and 71.5 nautical miles from China's Hainan island.
It also repeated its call for the rig to be withdrawn immediately and said it wanted negotiations as soon as possible.

"... we have requested that experts from the two countries meet as soon as possible, at any place, to discuss this," a Foreign Ministry spokesman said. "We hope that China will positively respond to this request."
Beijing has responded to Hanoi's repeated statements by saying that the area is its own territory and that its actions are beyond reproach.

China's main offshore oil company said last week that it had no immediate plans to move the rig from the area, which energy industry sources say may have commercially viable reserves of oil and associated gas.

"Any decision to leave the drilling area would be based on the drilling results," an official of the China National Offshore Oil Corp told Reuters. "Why should we leave the area? When the exploration is finished we will move the rig."

The two communist neighbours have competing claims on areas along their land border, on parts of the Tonkin Gulf and on the Paracel Island chain, which lie east of the latest area of dispute. They are also among six regional claimants to the Spratly Islands, which are further to the south.

Both sides have in recent years agreed to shelve some border problems and have worked hard to improve ties and boost border trade, but the temptation to exploit the oil-rich waters they dispute has been a constant threat to rapprochement.
Envoys from countries of the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN), a seven-member grouping which Vietnam joined in 1995, were briefed on the latest row by the Foreign Ministry in mid-March.

However, only one ASEAN country has so far backed Hanoi's call for China to withdraw the rig. A Thai diplomat said the right forum for the subject to be addressed was a scheduled ASEAN-China meeting in April.
